## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 3/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
State of the art (as of July 2026) in AI coding-agent governance and harness design — the problem space of the claude.md-workflow repo: project instruction files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style), lifecycle hooks, deterministic verification gates, persistent agent memory/working-state across sessions and compaction, behavioral guardrails against scope creep/overclaiming/sycophancy, git-level enforcement, task contracts, and parallel multi-agent orchestration (worktree isolation, orchestrator/reduce patterns, adversarial review). Survey and compare best practices from: Anthropic (Claude Code, Agent SDK, skills/hooks/subagents), OpenAI (Codex, AGENTS.md), Google (Gemini CLI/Jules/Antigravity), Microsoft (GitHub Copilot agents, AutoGen/agent frameworks), NVIDIA (agent toolkits/NeMo), xAI (Grok agents/coding); and non-Western labs: Moonshot AI (Kimi K2.5 agentic training), Zhipu/Z.ai (GLM-5.x coding agents), DeepSeek (agentic/tool-use practices), Tencent (recent Hunyuan model launch and agent tooling), MiniMax (M-series agentic models), Alibaba Qwen if relevant; plus respected independents: Nous Research (Hermes 4/Hermes agent), Fundamental Research Labs (Peter Wang co-founder), the team behind the Ornith-1.0 LLM, tinygrad/George Hotz's approach to minimal harnesses, and any other influential open agent-harness projects (e.g. OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Cline, Devin/Cognition). For each: what they prescribe for instruction-file structure and length, memory persistence, verification/eval gating, multi-agent patterns, and prompt-vs-deterministic enforcement. Identify convergent consensus, notable divergences (especially Western vs Chinese lab practices), and concrete, citable insights that should shape a 2026 rewrite of a drop-in governance kit for coding agents. Note if any named entity cannot be verified to exist (e.g. 'Ornith-1.0') rather than guessing.

## Claim under review
"GitHub's cloud coding agent defaults to deterministic permission-gating on every write action, with fully autonomous 'autopilot' mode as an explicit opt-in after trust is established."

**Source:** https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-app-the-agent-native-desktop-experience/ (primary)
**Supporting quote:** "By default, the cloud agent asks permission before each write action. Switch to autopilot once you have established trust."

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

# GitHub Copilot App Blog Post - Verification

**Page Status:** Yes, this page exists.

**Publication Date:** June 2, 2026

**Title:** "GitHub Copilot app: The agent-native desktop experience"

**Relevant Quote on Permission & Autopilot:**

"By default, the cloud agent asks permission before each write action. Switch to autopilot once you have established trust."

This statement appears in the section discussing cloud automations, explaining that the system requires user approval for write operations by default, with an option to enable autonomous execution after trust is established.

Web search results for query: "GitHub Copilot cloud agent "asks permission" "autopilot" write action default"

Links: [{"title":"Allowing GitHub Copilot CLI to work autonomously - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/autopilot"},{"title":"Application card: GitHub Copilot Agents - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents"},{"title":"Managing access to GitHub Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/cloud-agent/access-management"},{"title":"GitHub Copilot app: The agent-native desktop experience - The GitHub Blog","url":"https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-app-the-agent-native-desktop-experience/"},{"title":"GitHub Copilot | AI Assistant Documentation","url":"https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/copilot-agent.html"},{"title":"Configuring settings for GitHub Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/configuring-agent-settings"},{"title":"About GitHub Copilot cloud agent - GitHub Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/cloud-agent/about-cloud-agent"},{"title":"Responsible use of GitHub Copilot CLI - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/responsible-use/copilot-cli"},{"title":"Using v0.0.421 and when switching to autopilot the Enable autopilot mode dialog is gone · Issue #1810 · github/copilot-cli","url":"https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/1810"},{"title":"How to auto-approve workflow execution when Copilot coding agent run? · community · Discussion #162826","url":"https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/162826"}]

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about GitHub Copilot cloud agent permissions and autopilot:

## Default Behavior

By default, the cloud agent asks permission before each write action. Switch to autopilot once you have established trust.

## Autopilot and Permission Requests

It's important to note that autopilot mode and permission handling are separate concerns. Autopilot controls whether the agent pauses for your input between steps, not whether it asks for approval. Even in Autopilot, GitHub Copilot still requests approval before actions that require permission unless Allow All is turned on.

## Granting Permissions

For Copilot CLI (which has similar permission behavior to the cloud agent), you can change your mind later and grant full permissions, during an autopilot session, by using the /allow-all command (or its alias /yolo).

Typically, when you use Copilot CLI in autopilot mode, you will grant it full permissions to allow it to complete a task autonomously, without requiring you to approve activity as it works on the task.

The default behavior prioritizes safety by requiring explicit approval for write actions, with the option to switch to autopilot mode and grant permissions once you trust the agent's behavior.

GitHub Docs corroborate (docs.github.com pages on cloud agent settings and copilot-cli/autopilot): write actions require approval by default, and autopilot is an explicit mode switch.
